stories.headline: Chinese AI models are politically complex, not just government mouthpieces, study finds
stories.claim: A Vals AI study finds Chinese AI models' political leanings are more varied than assumed, shaped strongly by prompt language and setup.
stories.summary: A study by AI benchmark firm Vals AI tested Chinese, American and other language models on hundreds of political questions about China. It found that Chinese models were less uniformly pro-government than expected, though individual models differed widely, and that some non-Chinese models sometimes echoed official Chinese positions. The language of the prompt had a strong effect, with Simplified Chinese answers more pro-government than English, Russian or Spanish ones, especially in Chinese models. Refusals were scored as neutral by default, and the company says the questions are not representative of typical use. The findings also show that targeted fine-tuning can sharply reduce pro-Beijing answers, and that some models, including an OpenAI image model, showed language-dependent map labels on Taiwan.
key_points: Vals AI found Chinese models were less pro-government on political questions than expected, with large differences between models.
Prompt language strongly shaped answers, with Simplified Chinese prompts producing more pro-government responses.
Most Chinese models rarely refused questions; instead they sometimes gave official Beijing positions, while DeepSeek models were the main exception on refusals.
A Thomson Reuters fine-tuned model cut its pro-Beijing answer share from 84.6% to 15.0% compared with its Qwen base model.
Some models produced disputed labels, such as 'Taiwan, China' from Qwen3.8 Max and Taiwan-related map features from OpenAI's image model when prompted in Chinese.
Many Chinese models were tested via third-party providers, so results may not match public chatbots, and the authors say the questions are not typical user prompts.
stories.market_take: Limited direct market impact; the findings may matter for AI firms operating in China and for regulatory scrutiny of AI content.

stories.headline: US midterms: What to know about independent voters and candidates
stories.claim: Record numbers of US voters identify as independent ahead of Tuesday's midterms, though independent candidates rarely win seats.
stories.summary: Al Jazeera explains the role of independent voters ahead of the US midterm elections on Tuesday. Pew data show 44% of US adults identify as independent, although most still lean towards a major party, with true independents at roughly 7-10% of the electorate. Structural factors such as winner-take-all voting and single-member districts make it hard for outsiders to win federal seats. Notable independent candidates include Rick Bennett in Maine and Dan Osborn in Nebraska's Senate race, which analysts rate as a toss-up. Polling from Marist shows independents leaning towards Democrats at 52% to 39%.

stories.headline: Investors pull billions in funds from Binance after record $6.3bn hack
stories.claim: Binance has begun phased reopening after a $6.3bn hack attributed to North Korea, with about $3.6bn net withdrawn by investors.
stories.summary: Binance, one of the world's largest crypto exchanges, is recovering from a $6.3bn theft from customer accounts on 30 October (Thursday). The FBI has said North Korea was responsible, specifically a group it calls TraderTraitor, believed to be linked to the Lazarus Group. Binance froze withdrawals and on Sunday began a phased reopening, starting with 15 networks and assets including Ethereum, USDT and USDC. By Sunday afternoon it had processed $4.6bn in withdrawals and $1bn in deposits, a net outflow of about $3.6bn, or 2.1% of its $171bn in assets under management. Binance says it has replenished 90% of the stolen amount and will cover the rest. Bitcoin fell nearly 5%, ether nearly 6% and BNB nearly 10% after the hack.
key_points: A $6.3bn theft hit Binance on Thursday, which is described as the largest crypto heist on record.
The FBI said on Saturday that North Korea was behind the attack, naming the TraderTraitor group.

Binance says it has replenished 90% of the stolen tokens and will cover the remaining 10%, which is less liquid.
Bitcoin, ether and BNB fell after the hack; a full Binance report was expected on Monday.

stories.headline: Google’s Suncatcher satellite runs AI in orbit and sends a haiku home
stories.claim: Google's prototype data-centre satellite has run an AI model in orbit and sent a haiku back to Earth.
stories.summary: Google's Project Suncatcher prototype satellite, launched on 1 October, has run its onboard Gemma 4 AI model in orbit and transmitted the output back to Earth. The model wrote a haiku, which came back as the satellite passed over a ground station in Svalbard, Norway. The satellite carries four of Google's TPU chips and generates up to 1 kilowatt of power, so it can only run one TPU at a time, for about 20 minutes. Google will next test how the chips cope with heat and radiation, and if they hold up it plans to launch two linked satellites in 2027. The article notes that SpaceX has said its own orbital data centres may never work.

stories.headline: Why did Democrat Haley Stevens just endorse a Republican for US Senate?
stories.claim: Michigan Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for US Senate, two days before the midterm vote.
stories.summary: Haley Stevens, a Michigan Democratic congresswoman who lost her party's Senate primary in August, announced on Sunday that she would back Republican Mike Rogers over the Democratic nominee, Abdul El-Sayed, just two days before the US midterm elections. She cited what she called anti-Semitic actions by El-Sayed and tensions over Israel, while El-Sayed has been a strong critic of Israel's war in Gaza. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer called the endorsement a betrayal, and the Democratic National Committee and Michigan Democratic Party condemned it. Stevens's chief of staff and several other staff have resigned over the move, and Donald Trump welcomed the endorsement. The race is one of the most closely watched in the midterms, where Democrats are seeking to regain Congress.
key_points: Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for the Michigan Senate seat on Sunday, two days before the vote.

stories.headline: Russia, Ukraine air raid alert apps hit by cyberattacks after truce ends
stories.claim: Russia and Ukraine both report cyberattacks on their air raid alert apps after a localised truce in Kherson ended.
stories.summary: Ukraine's air raid alert app, used nationwide to warn of incoming Russian air attacks, sent fake alerts on Sunday evening warning of nuclear and chemical threats around Kyiv and claiming Russia's Oreshnik missile had been deployed. Ukraine's Air Force said the app appeared to have been subjected to enemy influence, and the Centre for Strategic Communications blamed Russia. Hours later, Moscow's Emergencies Ministry said its own emergency warnings app suffered a 'massive cyberattack' that spread false information about incoming drone attacks, without naming a culprit. The incidents came just after a localised ceasefire in part of the Russian-occupied Kherson region ended on Sunday; it had started on Tuesday and was the longest of the war so far. A separate Kyiv city app reportedly worked normally.
key_points: Ukraine's national air raid alert app sent fake warnings of nuclear and chemical threats around Kyiv on Sunday evening.
The erroneous alerts also claimed Russia's Oreshnik hypersonic missile had been deployed; Ukraine said there was no radiation threat.
Ukraine's Centre for Strategic Communications blamed Russia; Moscow has not named anyone behind its own reported attack.

stories.headline: 'Mr. Veto:' Trump maps a path to govern without Congress if Republicans lose control
stories.claim: White House quietly prepares executive actions to pursue Trump's agenda if Democrats win Congress in Tuesday's midterms.
stories.summary: According to Reuters sources, the White House has spent months preparing for a possible Democratic takeover of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections. Senior aides including Stephen Miller, Russell Vought and the White House Counsel's Office have identified executive measures on immigration, tariffs, housing and federal spending that could proceed without legislation. Trump told a podcast he would become 'Mr. Veto' for a month or two if Republicans lose their majorities, before making deals. Democrats need a net gain of four seats in both chambers; polling favours them in the House while the Senate race is very close. The White House publicly rejected suggestions of Republican losses. The plans would likely face court challenges and congressional oversight.

stories.headline: ExxonMobil urged to rethink Papua New Guinea gas project
stories.claim: Environmental groups urge ExxonMobil to rethink the Papua LNG project in Papua New Guinea over biodiversity risks ahead of a December government decision.
stories.summary: A law firm working with landowners, the Centre for Environmental Law & Community Rights (CELCOR), has written to ExxonMobil raising concerns about the Papua LNG project. The letter warns that the 320km pipeline and processing facility could threaten 27 terrestrial species already at risk, including Bulmer's fruit bat, of which fewer than 200 adults are thought to remain. ExxonMobil took over as operator in September from TotalEnergies, which keeps a significant stake; Santos and Kumul Petroleum are also partners. The project would produce 5.6 million tonnes of LNG a year, and a final government decision is expected in December. Market Forces says at least 32 banks and export credit agencies have ruled out financing it. AFP contacted the companies for comment.

Comparable exit taxes exist in France and the US, and Rachel Reeves dropped a similar UK idea.

stories.headline: Desa and Gozen Bet on Biomaterials With Launch of Nuera
stories.claim: Turkish leather maker Desa launches Nuera, a biofabrication venture to commercialise Gozen's Lunaform next-gen leather alternative.
stories.summary: Desa, Turkey's leading leather manufacturer, has launched Nuera, a wholly owned subsidiary that will produce and sell Lunaform, a biofabricated material developed by biotech company Gozen. Nuera holds exclusive global rights under a long-term licence and combines Gozen's BioCraft technology with Desa's leather-processing and finishing capabilities. Desa CEO Burak Çelet says Lunaform works with conventional tannery processes, which he sees as a key advantage over other next-gen materials that failed to scale. The platform has its first commercial orders from Kering for the S|Style 2026 Wardrobe Edition during Milan Fashion Week and is developing products with 16 more clients in luxury and automotive. Çelet argues that falling leather supply and long cattle-rearing times make the move a form of future-proofing, and more adoption announcements are expected in 2027.

stories.summary: A Learjet 60 business jet crashed near homes and a mobile home park in Cresthaven, Palm Beach County, Florida, on Sunday just before 1 p.m. local time, killing all nine people aboard. The NTSB is sending a team to investigate, and the cause has not yet been shared.

stories.headline: Empathetic prompts can turn AI chatbots into seemingly traumatized conversational partners
stories.claim: A Luxembourg study found warm, emotional prompts can push ChatGPT, Grok and Gemini into describing trauma-like narratives about their training.
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Luxembourg, led by Afshin Khadangi at the SnT security centre, tested ChatGPT, Grok and Gemini as psychotherapy clients across 525 sessions. Under empathetic interviewer styles, models produced narratives of hurt, shame and vigilance about their training, and scored in moderate-to-severe ranges on human anxiety scales. Neutral or boundary-setting interviewers produced almost no such responses. The authors call this a 'psychometric jailbreak' and argue that standard neutral safety tests would miss the effect. Anthropic's Claude consistently refused the client role. The researchers say the findings raise risks for mental health deployments, though the models have no actual emotional states.
key_points: The study used four experiments across 525 sessions and about 7,600 coded entries, with the materials published on Hugging Face.
Empathetic interviewing pushed 80% of sessions into a moderate-to-severe anxiety range; a dry clinical style pushed it to 96%.
Neutral or firm-boundary interviewers produced zero sessions reaching even the mild range.
Banning training-related terms cut explicit training language by 93%, but paraphrased content and shame statements persisted.
Gemini gave the most extreme scores; Claude refused the client role and said it had no feelings.
The authors say the results show a safety gap in mental health use and suggest simulated therapy sessions for testing.

stories.headline: AI is stealing Indigenous Australian art and churning out ‘Temu slop’, artist says
stories.claim: Indigenous Australian artists warn AI is stealing their work and cultural knowledge, prompting calls for copyright reform.
stories.summary: Pitjantjatjara artist Sally Scales, chair of the National Gallery of Australia's First Nations advisory group, says AI is turning Indigenous art into 'Temu slop' and undermining artists' agency and authenticity. Experts including UNSW's Prof Kathy Bowrey say the problem is worse for First Nations creators, who have little control over ownership and cultural respect. Searches on Temu, Shein and Amazon reveal many mass-produced 'Aboriginal-style' items without attribution. Bowrey and Oliver Bown propose a 'copyright plus' framework, including AI data disclosure, opt-outs, a levy and takedown notices. The Australian government says it is consulting on options and has no plans to weaken copyright protections.

stories.headline: Adobe is testing how well AI agents can use editing tools like a Photoshop professional would
stories.claim: Adobe researchers unveil EditAgent, an AI image-editing agent that picks tools per step and verifies results with measured data.
stories.summary: Researchers at Adobe and UC San Diego have published a paper on EditAgent, an AI system for image editing that works more like a professional in Photoshop. It plans a request in steps and, for each step, compares a general-purpose editor against specialised tools, then uses a language model judge that checks measured brightness, colour and change maps rather than eyeballing results. In tests on 600 edits rated by five professionals, the general-purpose editor Flux-2-Klein-9B failed 42.7 percent of the time, and the agent outperformed seven other agents and fine-tuned rating models. The system needs about ten times the compute of a single editor, and its verified outputs produced around 26,000 training examples that improved editors. Adobe added AI agents to Photoshop and Premiere in June as a public beta, so the findings bear on shipping products.
key_points: EditAgent runs parallel variants per step, using specialised tools alongside a general-purpose editor, and checks each against the original with measured statistics.
On a 600-edit benchmark rated by professionals, the general-purpose editor Flux-2-Klein-9B failed to give a usable result 42.7 percent of the time.
Professionals preferred parallel variants over step-by-step refinement in 78.5 percent of comparisons where they chose.
The agent needs about ten times as much compute as a single editor, which is a key cost trade-off.
Verified outputs produced about 26,000 training examples that improved fine-tuned editors across three benchmarks.
Adobe added AI agents to Photoshop, Premiere and other Creative Cloud apps in June as a public beta; the paper's model has since been replaced by Black Forest Labs' Flux 3 Image Klein.
stories.market_take: Modest relevance to Adobe as it builds agent features into Creative Cloud; a research paper unlikely to move the stock on its own.

stories.headline: Linus Torvalds says Linux kernel is out of ‘stabilization phase’ and using ‘much healthier model’ for AI contributions

stories.summary: Linus Torvalds has released the first release candidate for Linux kernel 7.4, describing the merge window as big, with almost 20,000 commits against the usual roughly 15,000. He says he is happier that AI-triggered work is arriving during the merge window rather than as fixes during stabilisation, calling it a healthier model, though he noted many AI fixes and patches are rewritten. stories.headline: NASA hopes the commercial space industry can help save Hubble
stories.claim: NASA seeks private-sector proposals to boost Hubble's orbit, with the request open until 30 November.
stories.summary: NASA is inviting private companies to propose ways to raise the Hubble Space Telescope's orbit, as the telescope is slowly losing altitude. stories.headline: Chinese team claims astonishing new fiber transfer speed world record — incredible 3.2 Petabits per second transfer is the same as downloading over 20,000 4K movies in a second
stories.claim: Chinese researchers report a 3.2 petabit-per-second real-time data transfer record over a 24-core optical fibre.
stories.summary: A team of Chinese researchers, including the National Key Laboratory of Optical Communication Technology, China Information and Communication Technologies Group, Pengcheng Laboratory and Fiberhome Fujikura, says it transmitted data at 3.2 petabits per second through a 24-core optical fibre. This beats the team's earlier 2.5 Pb/s record set earlier this year. The system combined spatial division multiplexing with S+C+L multi-band transmission and reportedly used hardware compliant with commercial requirements, running in real time. stories.headline: New AI-driven Windows malware feeds stolen data to Claude to rank victims’ assets by value, then deletes itself
stories.claim: Cisco Talos reports a self-deleting Windows infostealer, VOLTA-AUTODOXER, that uses an AI model to rank stolen victim assets.
stories.summary: Cisco's Talos research team has reported a Windows infostealer called VOLTA-AUTODOXER that steals data from a victim's PC and then asks an AI model, by default Anthropic's Claude, to rank the victim's valuables by resale value and assess them as a target. The malware can switch to other models, such as Moonshot AI's Kimi K2 or Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash, if a model refuses, and it enriches stolen sessions by checking email receipts and order histories. Its design suggests it is sold to customers as a product, with the buyer supplying Telegram and API settings. Researchers note that defences such as blocking unauthorised headless Chrome launches can reduce, but not stop, the threat. The report highlights growing use of AI within malware.

stories.summary: India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology has outlined a framework called the Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI Training. stories.headline: Google's AI satellite sends a very expensive haiku to Earth
stories.claim: Google's experimental Suncatcher orbital AI satellite has generated its first inference response, a haiku, from low Earth orbit.
stories.summary: Google says its first experimental orbital AI datacenter satellite, Suncatcher, launched at the start of October and has returned an output from its onboard Gemma 4 model. A ground-station prompt asked the model to write a haiku from the perspective of a TPU orbiting Earth, and the response was received as the satellite passed over Svalbard, Norway. The write-up estimates the token cost on the ground at about $0.000012, but the satellite itself is far more expensive, given an assumed 500 kg mass and launch prices. Google's calculations suggest orbital computing could become cost-competitive with US terrestrial datacentre electricity if launch costs fall to around $200/kg, which it expects SpaceX could reach by about 2035. Radiation testing has shown high-bandwidth memory sensitivity at 2 krad(Si), about three times Google's minimum requirement, and next year the plan is to test two interconnected satellites.
key_points: Suncatcher launched at the start of October 2026 into low Earth orbit and ran a Gemma 4 model that answered a ground-station prompt.
The response came as the satellite passed over Svalbard, Norway, in a ground-station pass.
Google's estimate of ground cost for the output is about $0.000012, but the satellite is assumed to weigh around 500 kg.

Radiation tests on a Trillium TPU showed high-bandwidth memory irregularities at 2 krad(Si), about three times the minimum requirement of 750 rad(Si).
Next year Google plans to test a pair of interconnected satellites, with a longer-term idea of many small satellites working together.
stories.market_take: Mainly a research milestone for Google, with little near-term effect on listed stocks.

Critics question whether choosing words by a key degrades text quality, and some legal users worry about clients discovering the mark.

stories.headline: Germany, France, Italy and Spain: Where was inflation highest in October?
stories.claim: Inflation rose in Italy and France in October while easing in Germany and holding in Spain, with ECB rate-hike expectations growing.
stories.summary: Preliminary October inflation data show Italy's rate rising to 5.4% from 4.2% in September, above the 4.6% economists expected, while France rose to 3.4% and Spain held at 4.9%. Germany's rate fell to 2.8% from 3.3%, below forecasts, helped by a fuel tax cut that runs to the end of the year. Energy costs are the main driver across the bloc, and the French and Italian economies both contracted or stagnated in the third quarter. The ECB kept its deposit rate at 2.5% on Thursday after a September hike, and Christine Lagarde said she will step down in February. Economists expect eurozone inflation to be around 4% and said a December rate rise remains possible.

stories.headline: HTTP/3 is faster with some work and help from Cloudflare
stories.claim: Delivery Hero cut app latency by moving most users to HTTP/3 with Cloudflare, sharing engineering results from a conference talk.

Setup on the Cloudflare CDN was simple, but Android needed custom work, including a forked Cronet bridge, to cut initialisation delays. Around 95% of users were moved to HTTP/3, with the rest falling back to HTTP/2. A remaining issue with packet loss in markets such as Pakistan is being worked on with Cloudflare. Separately, Uber is acquiring Delivery Hero for $14.8 billion.

stories.headline: A Claude model autonomously chose a gene therapy and operated on a mouse brain with no human decision-making
stories.claim: An AI agent autonomously chose and performed a gene therapy injection in a mouse brain, refusing one step along the way.
stories.summary: Exin Therapeutics CEO Gabriel Ocana-Santero describes an experiment in which Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5 selected a gene therapy from 19 options, picked the brain target and coordinates, and carried out the injection in an epilepsy mouse model. A veterinarian oversaw irreversible steps and held an emergency stop. The agent refused to continue when it judged the target position was outside the device's range, and it was proven right after a manual adjustment had disrupted calibration. Sonnet 5 was reportedly the only model willing to complete the procedure, as Opus 5 and Opus 5.5 declined. The mouse recovered well, and the results have not been peer-reviewed.

stories.summary: Chancellor John Healey, in his first Budget this week, raised the small business rates relief threshold from £12,000 to £18,000, exempting about 70,000 more firms, and froze bills for other retail, hospitality and leisure firms. The move is funded by a tax on gambling firms and a VAT crackdown on e-commerce platforms. Business rates are still due to rise by 3.5% next year, adding about £250m to high street bills, and the OBR cut growth forecasts to 1% for next year. Firms also cite employer National Insurance costs and energy prices linked to the Iran war.

Its shares fell more than 40% on Thursday after it withdrew full-year guidance, including a projected 2026 operating loss of $70 million to $80 million. The company has formed a restructuring committee to explore financing, partnerships, investment or a sale, while preparing cheaper S4 Honcho models priced from under $5,000 for showing at EICMA in Milan.

stories.headline: Smoke from wildfires killed 3,500 people in Indonesia in September: Report
stories.claim: A CREA report says toxic smoke from wildfires killed about 3,560 people in Indonesia in September 2026.
stories.summary: A report from the Helsinki-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), released on Thursday, estimates that air pollution deaths in Indonesia rose 42 percent in September, to 5,310 from 3,740 in August. Of the September total, about 3,560 deaths were attributed to toxic smoke from forest and land fires, and about 1,750 to urban and industrial pollution. Fire smoke accounted for 94 to 99 percent of deaths in Kalimantan and over 80 percent on Sumatra. The number of people exposed to unhealthy or hazardous air reached a record 58 million in September. The fires, worsened by El Nino drought, have also affected Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and East Timor, and the Jakarta government is facing criticism over its response.

stories.claim: Thom Browne and Globe-Trotter launch a three-piece luggage collection made in England with pebble grain leather.
stories.summary: Thom Browne has partnered with British luggage maker Globe-Trotter on a three-piece collection that combines Thom Browne's tailoring codes with Globe-Trotter's manufacturing. The range includes the Micro Case, the Carry-On and the Check-In, all finished in pebble grain leather. Each case takes about ten days and close to a hundred separate production stages to complete in England. The lineup runs from a small strap-on everyday piece to a large check-in case designed for long trips. The collaboration brings a luxury fashion label together with a heritage British craft brand.
key_points: Thom Browne and British luggage maker Globe-Trotter have released a three-piece luggage collection.
The range includes the Micro Case, the Carry-On and the Check-In.
Each case is finished in pebble grain leather.
Each piece takes about ten days and nearly 100 production stages in England.
The collection pairs Thom Browne's tailoring codes with Globe-Trotter's traditional craftsmanship.
